titulo: Spending the afternoon the way they spend it
subtitulo: The morning market, the evening walk, the match on in the bar — three things that are free and that no itinerary lists
cena: It is four in the afternoon, the museums are full, and the town looks asleep in a way that feels like there is nothing to do.
frasePiso: The best hours here are not on any itinerary. The market before noon, the square after six, and whatever is on in the bar.
decisao: trocar a terceira igreja da lista pelo mercado de manhã e pela praça às seis, que é onde a cidade realmente está

steps.pt: Italian towns have a rhythm, not opening hours. Morning is the market, afternoon is quiet, and from six the street fills up.
Start at the market. Not to buy dinner — to see what the season actually is and to talk to four people in eight minutes.

steps.acao: Do not touch the produce. Point and let them pick it.
steps.es: Dica signora, cosa le do? Guardi che pomodori.
steps.pt: Tell me, what can I give you? Look at these tomatoes.
steps.tts: Dica signora, cosa le do? Guardi che pomodori.

steps.promptPt: Ask what is in season right now. Speak now.
Order a small amount — enough for two people, today. Speak now.
steps.es: Me ne dia due etti, per favore.
steps.pinyin: meh neh DEE-a DOO-eh ET-tee per fa-VO-re
steps.pt: Give me two hundred grams, please.
steps.tts: Me ne dia due etti, per favore.

steps.pt: Un etto is a hundred grams and it is how food is bought here. Due etti of cheese is a normal, unembarrassing amount.

steps.promptPt: Ask to taste before committing, using the frame from B06. Speak now.

steps.pt: Then the evening walk. From six the whole town is outside, dressed, walking slowly, and going nowhere in particular.

steps.promptPt: Ask where people go for the evening walk. Speak now.
steps.es: Dove si fa la passeggiata la sera?
steps.pinyin: DO-ve see fa la pas-se-JA-ta la SE-ra
steps.pt: Where do people take the evening walk?
steps.tts: Dove si fa la passeggiata la sera?

steps.acao: Go at seven, not at five. Earlier and the street is still empty.
steps.es: Sul corso, verso le sette. Prima non c'è nessuno.
steps.pt: On the main street, around seven. Before that there's nobody.
steps.tts: Sul corso, verso le sette. Prima non c'è nessuno.

steps.promptPt: Ask whether anything is on this week. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is there any festival on this week?

steps.promptPt: The bar has the match on. Ask who is playing. Speak now.
Ask whether you can watch it there. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I watch the match here?

steps.promptPt: Ask which team is the local one, so you know who to sit with. Speak now.
steps.es: Qual è la squadra di qui?
steps.pinyin: kwal eh la SKWA-dra dee kwee
steps.tts: Qual è la squadra di qui?

steps.es: Cosa c'è di buono adesso? Me ne dia due etti, per favore. Dove si fa la passeggiata la sera?
steps.pinyin: KO-za cheh dee BWO-no a-DES-so. meh neh DEE-a DOO-eh ET-tee per fa-VO-re. DO-ve see fa la pas-se-JA-ta la SE-ra
steps.pt: Shadow the day: market, purchase, evening.
steps.tts: Cosa c'è di buono adesso? Me ne dia due etti, per favore. Dove si fa la passeggiata la sera?

steps.pt: I09 done. Market before noon, passeggiata from seven, the match in the bar — and etti is how you buy anything.

secoes.corpo: Un etto is one hundred grams. Due etti, tre etti — that is the unit for cheese, cured meat, olives and most things sold by weight. Asking for four hundred grams is understood but marks you instantly.
At a market stall the vendor picks. Handling the fruit yourself is a small breach with a large signal attached, and pointing does exactly the same job.

secoes.titulo: The passeggiata is real and it has a clock
secoes.corpo: In most towns the evening walk starts around six or seven and runs along one particular street or square that everybody knows. Going at the wrong hour or on the wrong street is why some visitors conclude it does not happen anymore.

secoes.titulo: The match is a way in
secoes.corpo: Asking which team is the local one, before saying anything about football, is the single easiest conversation opener available in a bar. The answer is never neutral and is always given at length.

permissao: You are allowed to skip the third church. Spending an afternoon at a market and an evening walking a street with everyone else is not a failure to sightsee — it is the part of the trip you will still be able to describe in five years.
espelho: Anyone who has come home from a trip remembering the ordinary afternoon better than the monument they queued ninety minutes for already knows what this part argues. The itinerary is easier to justify; it is just rarely what stays.

fichasCulturais.sinal: At four in the afternoon the town is shuttered and empty, and it looks as though nothing is happening and nothing will.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: This place is dead, or everything interesting is closed to visitors.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The Italian day has a trough in the middle of the afternoon and a peak in the early evening. What you are seeing is not the town at rest for the day — it is the town between its two busy periods.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Use the trough the way locals do, then be on the main street or the square from around seven. The same emptiness fills completely.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop scheduling your evenings as though the day ends at six, and you see the hours when the place is most itself.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not in the largest tourist centres, where the rhythm has largely flattened out, and not in August in a town that has emptied for the holidays — there the quiet really is quiet.
